name: Eurodance
description: High-energy dance music with catchy hooks, pounding kicks, and Euro-style synth leads. Popularised in the 90s by artists like Haddaway, Snap! and Ace of Base.
key: Minor keys (e.g. A minor, D minor)

parts.name: Kick
tips: Use a tight, punchy 4-on-the-floor kick pattern (every beat).
Layer a sub-bass sine click underneath the kick for body.
Keep the kick around 60–80 Hz fundamental with a sharp transient.
Sidechain compression from kick to bass for a pumping effect.

parts.name: Bass
tips: A short, staccato synth bass playing on the off-beats or 16th-note runs.
Use a sawtooth or square wave with a fast attack and medium decay.
Keep the bassline simple — root note on beat 1, octave jumps for energy.
Roll off everything below 50 Hz and above 400 Hz to sit cleanly.

parts.name: Snare / Clap
tips: Clap or snare on beats 2 and 4, often layered for a thick crack.
Add a snare roll leading into the chorus or drop.
Use reverb with a short tail (0.4–0.8 s) for a stadium feel.
Pitch the snare up slightly for brightness in higher-energy sections.

parts.name: Hi-Hats
tips: Straight 8th-note closed hi-hats to drive momentum.
Open hi-hat on the upbeat of beat 4 before the kick.
Automate the hi-hat volume for subtle groove variations.
Keep velocity slightly random to avoid a mechanical feel.

parts.name: Lead Synth
tips: Detuned supersaw or saw-stack patch for that classic Euro sound.
Use a portamento/glide setting for smooth note-to-note movement.
Add a chorus and a stereo enhancer to widen the sound.
Drive through a light distortion or saturation for edge.

parts.name: Pad / Chord
tips: Lush, wide chord pads that fill the mid-range without muddying.
Use a slow attack (200–400 ms) so chords bloom behind the lead.
Pan slightly left and right to create width and space.
High-pass everything below 200 Hz on the pad to keep the low end clean.

parts.name: Vocal Hook
tips: A short, catchy 4-bar melody that repeats every 8–16 bars.
Add tight delay (1/8 note) and moderate reverb for gloss.
Use pitch correction (subtle) and doubling for a polished sound.
Keep the hook in the chorus and strip it back in verses.

parts.name: Structure
tips: Intro (8 bars) → Verse (16 bars) → Pre-chorus (8 bars) → Chorus (16 bars) → Bridge → Chorus out.
Drop all elements except kick for 2 bars before the main chorus for impact.
Use a riser synth or snare roll in the last 4 bars before each chorus.
Outro fades or ends with a reverse crash and silence.

name: Trap
description: Dark, hard-hitting beats defined by rolling hi-hats, 808 bass, and cinematic atmospheres. Rooted in Atlanta hip-hop and now spanning multiple subgenres.

parts.name: 808 Bass
tips: Use an 808 sample pitched to the key of your track.
Long sustain with a slow release — let it ring under the melody.
Sidechain the 808 to the kick for tightness, but keep a pumping feel.
Distort or saturate lightly to cut through on small speakers.

parts.name: Kick
tips: Short, hard kick — usually on beat 1 with syncopated hits.
Layer a click sample with a deep punchy thud.
Keep kick transients sharp — use a limiter/clipper on the kick bus.
Avoid clashing with the 808 frequency-wise; high-pass one or the other.

parts.name: Hi-Hats
tips: Rapid triplet/sextuplet hi-hat rolls are the signature of trap.
Vary velocity heavily for a human, bouncing feel.
Automate roll speed — slow in verses, rapid rolls building to the drop.
Use a closed hat with a very short decay and high pitch.

parts.name: Snare
tips: Sparse snare placement — often only on beat 3, or skipped entirely.
Clap layers add texture; use 3–4 layered clap samples.
Long reverb tail (1–2 s) for that atmospheric, cave-like sound.
Pitch the snare to match the key subtly.

parts.name: Melody / Lead
tips: Dark, eerie melodies — flute, bells, strings or synth plucks.
Keep melodic phrases short (2–4 bars) and looping.
Use pentatonic or chromatic notes for tension.
Add subtle pitch vibrato to a melodic lead for authenticity.

parts.name: FX & Atmosphere
tips: Risers, whooshes, and impacts between sections.
Reversed cymbal or pad before a drop for anticipation.
Sub-bass rumble in quiet sections for tension.
Vinyl crackle or cassette noise on a very low volume for texture.

parts.name: Structure
tips: Intro (4–8 bars) → Verse → Hook → Verse → Hook → Bridge → Hook out.
Keep hooks minimal so they hit harder in contrast to the verse.
Mute the 808 and kick for 1 bar for a 'breathing' moment.
End drops with silence or a reversed crash for drama.

name: Deep House
description: Soulful, hypnotic house music with warm chord progressions, rolling basslines, and subtle groove. Think late-night dance floors and silky vocals.
key: Minor or Dorian mode (warm, soulful feel)

parts.name: Kick
tips: Soft, deep 4-on-the-floor kick with subtle low-mid warmth.
Avoid sharp transients — aim for a thud, not a crack.
Keep the kick consistent but automate velocity for groove.
Compress gently with a slow attack so the transient breathes.

parts.name: Bass
tips: Rolling, melodic bass with movement every 2–4 bars.
Use a round, warm synth bass or sampled upright bass.
Sidechain lightly so the bass ducks slightly under the kick.
Add subtle filter modulation to give the bassline life.

parts.name: Chords
tips: Jazz-influenced chords: 7ths, 9ths, and 11ths.
Stab chords on the off-beat (every upbeat) for rhythmic movement.
Use a warm electric piano, Rhodes, or soft synth pad.
Spread chords wide in the stereo field.

parts.name: Hi-Hats
tips: Subtle, swung 16th-note hi-hats with light velocity variation.
Open hi-hat on the upbeat of beat 4 is classic deep house.
Keep hats low in the mix — they support groove, not dominate.
Add gentle reverb to blend hats into the mix.

parts.name: Vocal
tips: Breathy, intimate vocal — often chopped into rhythmic stabs.
Use soulful ad-libs and whispers as texture.
Delay throws on select words add a hypnotic feel.
Keep vocals low-key in the mix; they float over rather than dominate.

parts.name: FX & Atmosphere
tips: Subtle atmospheric pads and ambient textures underneath everything.
Use long reverb tails (2–4 s) on pads to create spaciousness.
Add an occasional shaker or tambourine for organic feel.
Filter sweeps slowly throughout the track for movement.

parts.name: Structure
tips: Long intro (16–32 bars) to build the atmosphere slowly.
Elements gradually introduced every 8–16 bars.
Breakdown: strip to just kick and bass, then rebuild.
Deep house is about the journey — avoid abrupt transitions.

name: Drum & Bass
description: Fast-paced electronic music built around breakbeats and heavy sub-bass. Originating from UK rave culture, it spans liquid, neurofunk, jungle, and more.

parts.name: Breakbeat
tips: Start from a classic break (Amen, Think Break, Apache) and chop it up.
Use time-stretching to pitch and time-match to your project BPM.
Layer additional claps, kicks and snares for punch.
Use a compressor on the break bus with a fast attack to glue the layers.

parts.name: Sub Bass
tips: Deep, heavy sub — use a sine wave or round-edged waveform.
Reese bass (detuned saws with heavy modulation) for neurofunk flavor.
Alternate between held notes and faster modulated bass for variation.
High-pass above 30 Hz to avoid subsonic rumble.

parts.name: Mid Bass / Reese
tips: A distorted, growling mid-range bass is a DnB staple.
Use multiple detuned oscillators with heavy filter modulation.
Automate the filter cutoff to create movement and tension.
Layer with a sub bass (separate channel) for full spectrum coverage.

parts.name: Pads & Atmosphere
tips: Dark, evolving pads in the background for depth.
For liquid DnB: warm, lush pads and melodic strings.
For neurofunk: cold, metallic textures and sci-fi atmospheres.
Use long reverb and modulation to make pads feel huge.

parts.name: Lead / Melody
tips: Liquid DnB: Rhodes, piano, and lush synth leads.
Neurofunk: glitchy, distorted synth leads with heavy processing.
Keep melodies relatively simple — the rhythm does the heavy lifting.
Use a 1/4 or dotted 1/8 delay to create call-and-response phrases.

parts.name: Structure
tips: Intro (16 bars of atmosphere) → Build → Drop → Breakdown → Drop 2 → Outro.
The 'drop' is the full break + bass hitting simultaneously.
Halftime sections (8 bars) where the break plays at half-speed for contrast.
Use silence or a single high note before drops for maximum impact.

name: Lo-Fi Hip-Hop
description: Mellow, sample-based hip-hop defined by warm tape saturation, dusty drums, and jazzy chords. Perfect study and relaxation music.
key: Major or Dorian (warm and nostalgic feel)

parts.name: Drums
tips: Swung or shuffled 808 or vintage drum machine samples.
Kick on beat 1, light snare on beat 2 and 4 with ghost notes.
Humanise the hi-hats — vary velocity and add micro-timing offsets.
Apply vinyl crackle or tape saturation on the drum bus.

parts.name: Chords / Sample
tips: Sample jazz, soul, or bossa nova records — chop and loop 2–4 bars.
Or program Rhodes/Wurlitzer chords with jazz extensions (7, 9, 11).
Apply a low-pass filter to roll off the highs for a warm, muffled sound.
Pitch the sample slightly sharp or flat (+/- 20 cents) for character.

parts.name: Bass
tips: Simple, melodic bass following the chord root notes.
Electric bass sample or a round synth bass with subtle saturation.
Keep the bass laid-back — slightly behind the beat.
Low-pass filter at around 500–800 Hz for a muffled, warm tone.

parts.name: Melody
tips: Soft piano or flute melody playing a simple 2–4 bar loop.
Leave space in the melody — lo-fi is about breathing room.
Add slight pitch wobble via automation to simulate tape wow and flutter.
Use a room reverb with pre-delay for a close, intimate sound.

parts.name: Texture & FX
tips: Vinyl crackle sample looped underneath everything.
Rain, cafe, or city ambience on a separate low-volume track.
Tape saturation plugin on the master bus (RC-20, Vinyl Distortion).
Subtle pitch modulation (LFO on tune) to simulate cassette wobble.

parts.name: Structure
tips: Lo-fi tracks are often minimal — just a loop with subtle variation.
Introduce elements slowly every 8 bars: first drums, then bass, then chords.
Keep the song short (2–3 mins) or loop endlessly for study playlists.
Variation is light: add a hi-hat fill here, mute the bass there.
